## Why

The leg scout searches Atlas Obscura for unusual places along the drive, but it can't check what it finds. A hook refuses any leg scout search that isn't limited to `atlasobscura.com`, and the leg scout has no `WebFetch`. Atlas Obscura blocks `WebFetch` with a 403, so the leg scout never reads the place's page. All it gets is what the search returns. That's enough to find a place, but not to tell whether it's worth recommending.

Example, from a search run on 2026-10-29 for "Big Sur California unusual places", limited to atlasobscura.com. `WebSearch` returned two parts:

- **A list of 10 links, each with only a title and a URL,** such as "McWay Falls and Waterfall House Ruins in Big Sur". There's no snippet, address, or coordinates for each link.
- **One summary the search tool wrote about all the results.** It described 5 places. One line said "The park was closed as of March 2019 due to storm damage, so check current status." Two of the 5 places it described, the Henry Miller Memorial Library and Nepenthe, had no link in the list.

So the leg scout can't check whether McWay Falls is open now. The stay researcher can, since it has general web search and `WebFetch`.

Nothing in the design or the research says why the leg scout was limited to Atlas Obscura. The limit was in the first draft of technical spec 6.2, on 2026-10-10, with no reason given. The research (`research/data-sources-attractions.md`, section 5) compared general search with Atlas Obscura search. It didn't ask whether the leg scout needs general search. A design walkthrough on 2026-10-11 (`reviews/walkthroughs/findings-1.md`, F3) found that the hook stopped the leg scout from checking a seasonal closure on the Moab Day 4 drive. Seasonal closures were then left to the worker's judgment, and the hook stayed. Joe decided on 2026-10-29 in chat to give the leg scout the same web tools as the stay researcher.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 6.2 (the leg scout) and 6.5 (the hook).
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), section 3 (which agent gets which tool) and section 4 (the hook).
- [Web search design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/data-sources/web-search.md), sections 1 to 3.

## Open questions

- ~~What does the leg scout use general web search for? Proposal: only to check leads and details, such as whether a place is open, a seasonal closure, or hours Google doesn't have. Not to find more places. `search_along_leg` already finds the mainstream places along the drive, and Atlas Obscura finds the unusual ones. A "must-see things to do" search for each town on the drive would add searches without adding much.~~ Settled on 2026-10-30 in chat: check only (see "Do").

## Do

- Give the leg scout general `WebSearch` and `WebFetch`, as the stay researcher has, in its definition (`src/agent/leg-scout-definition.ts`) and in tool design section 3's table. Decided on 2026-10-29 in chat.
- Remove the hook that limits the leg scout's search to Atlas Obscura: `src/agent/web-search-hook.ts`, its test, its entry in `src/agent/worker-hooks.ts`, and `webSearchDomainsSchema` in `src/agent/worker-hook-input.schema.ts`. Take it out of tool design section 4 and technical spec 6.5. Decided on 2026-10-29 in chat.
- Change the leg scout's instructions (`src/agent/leg-scout-prompt.ts`) and technical spec 6.2 to say:
  - Atlas Obscura finds leads. The search tool's summary describes them, and a place it describes may have no link.
  - Check each lead with `find_place` and `search_along_leg`, and on the web when something needs checking, such as "closed as of March 2019".
  - Use general web search only to check leads and details, such as whether a place is open, a seasonal closure, or hours Google doesn't have. Don't use it to find more places. Why: the problem this issue fixes is that the leg scout can't check what it finds. `search_along_leg` already finds the mainstream places along the drive, and Atlas Obscura the unusual ones, and no run has shown the leg scout missing good places. A rule for finding places on the web can come later if a run shows the need, such as a stop for "the best barbecue on the way", which Google ranks badly. Settled on 2026-10-30 in chat.
  - Check only enough to recommend the place or skip it. The user can ask for more. Don't read up on a place's history or background.
  - A place's source link is its Atlas Obscura page when the search listed one, or else the page the check found.
- Fix the line in the leg scout's instructions that says "If Google doesn't list it, look up the street address from the search result instead." A search result has no address. Say instead: when `find_place` doesn't list it, try a shorter or plainer name, with the town, such as "McWay Falls" for "McWay Falls and Waterfall House Ruins". Drop the place only if that fails too. Give the stay researcher's instructions (`src/agent/stay-researcher-prompt.ts`) the same fallback, since it can't read Atlas Obscura pages either. From a review note on #215, settled on 2026-10-29 in chat.
- Correct web search design sections 1 and 3 on what `WebSearch` returns: links with only a title and a URL, plus one summary over all the results, which may describe places that have no link. Section 3 says the search gives "a one-line description" for each place.

## Done when

- A real leg scout run on San Francisco Day 2 (domain model, section 5.1) searches Atlas Obscura, checks a lead on the web, and adds candidates with detour times.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.
